Written as literal UTF-8 glyphs; this file is valid UTF-8, which Roslyn's\n        // BOM-less source detection decodes as UTF-8, so the literals compile to exactly these chars.","originalFile":"using Guardrails.Core.Graph;\n\nnamespace Guardrails.Core.Tests;\n\n/// <summary>\n/// Unit tests for <see cref=\"HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render\"/> (issue #33): the self-contained local\n/// <c>diagram.html</c> viewer. Pure string mapping — no disk. Pins the provenance line, the\n/// verbatim-source embedding, the interaction prerequisites (loose security for clicks, pan/zoom,\n/// fullscreen), determinism, and newline normalization.\n/// </summary>\npublic sealed class HtmlDiagramRendererTests\n{\n    private const string Hash = \"abc123def456\";\n    private const string Source = \"flowchart TD\\n  task_a[\\\"a\\\"]:::task\\n  classDef task fill:#cfe8ff;\";\n\n    private static readonly IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string> NoTargets =\n        new Dictionary<string, string>(StringComparer.Ordinal);\n\n    private static readonly IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string> OneTarget =\n        new Dictionary<string, string>(StringComparer.Ordinal) { [\"task_01_a\"] = \"tasks/01-a/\" };\n\n    [Fact]\n    public void Render_FirstLine_IsProvenanceComment_WithSameHash()\n    {\n        string html = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, NoTargets);\n        string firstLine = html.Split('\\n')[0];\n\n        // Same provenance shape as diagram.md, and FIRST so the \\A-anchored reader (graph --check)\n        // matches it in both files.\n        Assert.Equal($\"<!-- guardrails:graph v1 source-sha256={Hash} -->\", firstLine);\n    }\n\n    [Fact]\n    public void Render_EmbedsSourceVerbatim_InRawTextScript()\n    {\n        string html = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, NoTargets);\n\n        Assert.Contains(\"type=\\\"text/plain\\\"\", html);\n        Assert.Contains(Source, html); // verbatim — not interpolated into a JS string\n        Assert.Contains(\"<!doctype html>\", html);\n    }\n\n    [Fact]\n    public void Render_EnablesClicksAndNavigation()\n    {\n        string html = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, NoTargets);\n\n        // Clicks (node -> source file) only fire when mermaid runs in 'loose' security.\n        Assert.Contains(\"securityLevel: 'loose'\", html);\n        // Pan/zoom + fullscreen affordances.\n        Assert.Contains(\"svg-pan-zoom\", html);\n        Assert.Contains(\"requestFullscreen\", html);\n    }\n\n    [Fact]\n    public void Render_RaisesMermaidSizeCeilings_SoLargeDagsRender()\n    {\n        // Issue #108: a large plan's DAG source exceeds Mermaid's default 50 000-char maxTextSize\n        // and/or 500-edge maxEdges ceiling, so mermaid.render throws and the page falls back to\n        // \"could not render\". The fix lifts BOTH ceilings in mermaid.initialize — assert they are\n        // present (a regression that drops either re-introduces the big-plan render failure).\n        string html = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, NoTargets);\n\n        Assert.Contains(\"maxTextSize: 5000000\", html);\n        Assert.Contains(\"maxEdges: 100000\", html);\n    }\n\n    [Fact]\n    public void Render_IsDeterministic()\n    {\n        Assert.Equal(\n            HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, OneTarget),\n            HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, OneTarget));\n    }\n\n    [Fact]\n    public void Render_NormalizesCrlf_NoCarriageReturnsInOutput()\n    {\n        string html = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(\"flowchart TD\\r\\n  a-->b\\r\\n\", Hash, NoTargets);\n        Assert.DoesNotContain('\\r', html);\n    }\n\n    [Fact]\n    public void Render_EmptyHash_Throws()\n    {\n        Assert.Throws<ArgumentException>(() => HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, \"\", NoTargets));\n    }\n\n    [Fact]\n    public void Render_NullTaskFolderTargets_Throws()\n    {\n        Assert.Throws<ArgumentNullException>(() => HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, null!));\n    }\n\n    // === legend overlay (outside the Mermaid graph; see MermaidRenderer remarks) =======\n\n    [Fact]\n    public void Render_IncludesALegendOverlayDiv_OutsideTheEmbeddedMermaidSource()\n    {\n        // A Mermaid-native legend was prototyped and rendered broken headless (dagre treats a\n        // disconnected subgraph as a phantom extra \"task\"); the only working placement is an HTML\n        // overlay div outside the embedded Mermaid <script> source, mirroring #bar/#hint.\n        string html = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, NoTargets);\n\n        Assert.Contains(\"id=\\\"legend\\\"\", html, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n    }\n\n    [Fact]\n    public void Render_LegendOverlay_StatesBothAColorAndABeforeAfterTimingWord()\n    {\n        // A bare category name would not preserve the \"preflights run before, guardrails run\n        // after\" semantic the removed nested boxes used to convey visually — the legend must spell\n        // out both the colour mapping AND the timing/consequence in words.\n        string html = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, NoTargets);\n\n        Assert.Contains(\"Preflight\", html, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        Assert.Contains(\"Guardrail\", html, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        Assert.Contains(\"BEFORE\", html, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        Assert.Contains(\"AFTER\", html, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n    }\n\n    [Fact]\n    public void Render_LegendOverlay_IsNotInsideTheEmbeddedGraphSourceScript()\n    {\n        // The legend must live OUTSIDE the raw-text <script id=\"graph-source\"> element — it is\n        // not part of the Mermaid source, so it can never affect anything that parses that source\n        // (rendering) or hashes it (GraphSourceHash, via MermaidRenderer.SemanticContent).\n        string html = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, NoTargets);\n\n        int scriptStart = html.IndexOf(\"id=\\\"graph-source\\\"\", StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        int scriptEnd = html.IndexOf(\"</script>\", scriptStart, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        string scriptContent = html[scriptStart..scriptEnd];\n\n        Assert.DoesNotContain(\"legend\", scriptContent, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n    }\n\n    // === task-container title-band overlay (issue #232/#233 superseded, issue #235) ====\n    //\n    // The Mermaid-source anchor-node mechanism (#211) proved useless in practice — a real\n    // headless-Chrome measurement found the anchor covering only 0.44% of a content-dense\n    // container's area, off-center, missed by every realistic click point. The fix instead\n    // injects a post-render SVG overlay on the container's title/label band via JavaScript.\n\n    [Fact]\n    public void Render_EmbedsTaskFolderTargets_AsJsonSideTable()\n    {\n        string html = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, OneTarget);\n\n        Assert.Contains(\"id=\\\"task-folder-targets\\\"\", html, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        Assert.Contains(\"\\\"task_01_a\\\"\", html, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        Assert.Contains(\"tasks/01-a/\", html, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n    }\n\n    [Fact]\n    public void Render_NoLongerEmitsAnchorNodeMechanism()\n    {\n        // The #211 anchor-node click mechanism (Mermaid-source invisible node + classDef) is\n        // superseded entirely — HtmlDiagramRenderer must not reference it either.\n        string html = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, OneTarget);\n\n        Assert.DoesNotContain(\"classDef invisible\", html, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n    }\n\n    [Fact]\n    public void Render_OverlayScript_AppendsToCluster_NotInsertsFirst()\n    {\n        // Load-bearing z-order fix: appendChild (not insertBefore as firstChild) — see class\n        // remarks and HtmlDiagramRenderer's remarks for why insertBefore silently blocks clicks\n        // (it lands the overlay BEHIND the cluster's own background rect).\n        string html = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, OneTarget);\n\n        Assert.Contains(\"cluster.appendChild(a)\", html, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        Assert.DoesNotContain(\"insertBefore(a, cluster.firstChild\", html, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n    }\n\n    [Fact]\n    public void Render_OverlayScript_ComputesBandFromClusterAndLabelBBox()\n    {\n        string html = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, OneTarget);\n\n        Assert.Contains(\"cluster.getBBox()\", html, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        Assert.Contains(\"label.getBBox()\", html, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        Assert.Contains(\".cluster-label\", html, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n    }\n\n    [Fact]\n    public void Render_OverlayScript_UsesTransparentFill_NotNone()\n    {\n        // Same hit-testing hazard as the retired anchor node: fill:none is invisible to\n        // pointer-events:visiblePainted hit-testing; the overlay rect must use a painted-but-\n        // invisible transparent fill instead.\n        string html = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, OneTarget);\n\n        Assert.Contains(\"'transparent'\", html, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n    }\n\n    [Fact]\n    public void Render_OverlayScript_SetsFillViaInlineStyle_NotTheFillAttribute()\n    {\n        // Real-browser regression (found live, not guessed): Mermaid's own generated stylesheet\n        // carries a rule shaped like `#dag .cluster rect{fill:<theme color>;...}`. Since the\n        // overlay rect is nested inside the .cluster group, that selector matches it too — and a\n        // CSS class/tag selector beats a plain HTML presentation attribute, so\n        // `rect.setAttribute('fill', 'transparent')` was silently overridden, painting a solid\n        // theme-colored bar over the container's title text (confirmed via getComputedStyle:\n        // attribute said \"transparent\", computed fill was the theme's cluster-background color).\n        // An inline style (`rect.style.fill = ...`) wins over any external/embedded stylesheet\n        // rule short of `!important`, so it reliably stays invisible. This test would have caught\n        // the regression: `Assert.Contains(\"'transparent'\")` alone passes for EITHER form.\n        string html = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, OneTarget);\n\n        Assert.Contains(\"rect.style.fill = 'transparent'\", html, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        Assert.DoesNotContain(\"rect.setAttribute('fill'\", html, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n    }\n\n    [Fact]\n    public void Render_OverlayScript_RunsAfterMermaidRenderResolves()\n    {\n        string html = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, OneTarget);\n\n        int renderCall = html.IndexOf(\"await mermaid.render(\", StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        int overlayDefinition = html.IndexOf(\"function addTaskContainerOverlays\", StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        Assert.True(renderCall >= 0 && overlayDefinition >= 0, \"both the render call and overlay function must be present\");\n\n        // The overlay must be INVOKED after the render call (the definition itself may appear\n        // earlier in the script — only invocation order matters for correctness).\n        int overlayInvocation = html.IndexOf(\"addTaskContainerOverlays(\", renderCall, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        Assert.True(overlayInvocation > renderCall, \"the overlay must be applied to the SVG mermaid.render just produced\");\n    }\n\n    [Fact]\n    public void Render_EmptyTaskFolderTargets_StillRendersValidPage()\n    {\n        string html = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, NoTargets);\n\n        Assert.Contains(\"id=\\\"task-folder-targets\\\"\", html, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        Assert.Contains(\"{}\", html, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n    }\n\n    // === long task-name title wrap-overflow fix (issue cluster-label-wrap-overflow) ====\n    //\n    // Mermaid always wraps a cluster's title <div> to a hardcoded 200px width (bundled\n    // mermaid@11.4.1's plain flowchart cluster shape never overrides createText's width=200\n    // default), and dagre's layout pass reserves the container's header-strip height BEFORE that\n    // wrapped height is known — so a long kebab-case task name that wraps to 2+ lines prints past\n    // the reserved strip, overlapping the first leaf guardrail/preflight box below it. No Mermaid\n    // config knob avoids this (verified against the bundled 11.4.1 source). The fix re-wraps the\n    // SAME text at up to the container's own (already wider) width post-render instead, verified\n    // headless against 8+ real plans (40+ long task names, container widths ~230px-~1100px,\n    // wraps of 2-3 lines): every case converged to one line with the same healthy gap a\n    // never-wrapped label already has, and every already-fits label was left byte-for-byte\n    // unchanged (including the whole golden hello-guardrails example).\n\n    [Fact]\n    public void Render_DefinesFixWrappedClusterLabelsFunction()\n    {\n        string html = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, OneTarget);\n\n        Assert.Contains(\"function fixWrappedClusterLabels(svgEl)\", html, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n    }\n\n    [Fact]\n    public void Render_WrapFix_RunsAfterMermaidRenderResolves_AndBeforeTheOverlay()\n    {\n        // Ordering is load-bearing: addTaskContainerOverlays measures the label's CURRENT bbox to\n        // size its click band, so a label the wrap fix already shrank back to one line must be\n        // fixed FIRST, or the band would be sized for the original (possibly multi-line) wrap.\n        string html = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, OneTarget);\n\n        int renderCall = html.IndexOf(\"await mermaid.render(\", StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        int wrapFixInvocation = html.IndexOf(\"fixWrappedClusterLabels(\", renderCall, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        int overlayInvocation = html.IndexOf(\"addTaskContainerOverlays(\", renderCall, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n\n        Assert.True(renderCall >= 0 && wrapFixInvocation > renderCall && overlayInvocation > renderCall,\n            \"both post-render fixes must be invoked after the render call\");\n        Assert.True(wrapFixInvocation < overlayInvocation,\n            \"the wrap fix must run BEFORE the title-band overlay so the band reflects the corrected label size\");\n    }\n\n    [Fact]\n    public void Render_WrapFix_MeasuresViaScrollWidth_NotGetBoundingClientRect()\n    {\n        // Regression guard for the exact measurement pitfall this fix's own investigation hit:\n        // getBoundingClientRect() reports on-screen pixels affected by the page's pan-zoom\n        // transform, which is misleading when compared against a foreignObject's local width/\n        // height attributes. scrollWidth/scrollHeight are local layout-box measurements, in the\n        // SAME coordinate system as those attributes, regardless of the current zoom level.\n        string html = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, OneTarget);\n\n        int fnStart = html.IndexOf(\"function fixWrappedClusterLabels\", StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        int fnEnd = html.IndexOf(\"\\n}\\n\", fnStart, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        string fnBody = html[fnStart..fnEnd];\n\n        Assert.Contains(\"div.scrollWidth\", fnBody, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        Assert.Contains(\"div.scrollHeight\", fnBody, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        Assert.DoesNotContain(\"getBoundingClientRect\", fnBody, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n    }\n\n    [Fact]\n    public void Render_WrapFix_NeverNarrowsBelowMermaidsOriginalWidth()\n    {\n        // The fix only ever WIDENS a label (fewer lines needs less height, never more) — it must\n        // never choose a width narrower than what Mermaid already assigned, which would be a\n        // regression risking MORE wrapping, not less.\n        string html = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, OneTarget);\n\n        Assert.Contains(\"Math.max(currentWidth, clusterBox.width - 16)\", html, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n    }\n\n    [Fact]\n    public void Render_WrapFix_SkipsLabelsThatAlreadyFitOnOneLine()\n    {\n        // Short names (e.g. every task in the golden hello-guardrails example) must be left\n        // completely untouched — this is the guard that makes that a no-op.\n        string html = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, OneTarget);\n\n        Assert.Contains(\"if (naturalWidth <= currentWidth) continue;\", html, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n    }\n\n    [Fact]\n    public void Render_WrapFix_RevertsWhenWideningDoesNotReduceHeight()\n    {\n        // A container too narrow to help must fall back to Mermaid's original sizing rather than\n        // risk an oddly-proportioned label — never regress relative to the pre-fix rendering.\n        string html = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, OneTarget);\n\n        Assert.Contains(\"if (newHeight >= currentHeight)\", html, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        Assert.Contains(\"div.setAttribute('style', savedInline);\", html, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n    }\n\n    [Fact]\n    public void Render_WrapFix_RecentersTheLabelOnTheSameMidpointAfterWidening()\n    {\n        // Mermaid centers the label group via translate(x - bbox.width / 2, y); widening without\n        // re-centering would shift the (now wider) box off-center over the cluster.\n        string html = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, OneTarget);\n\n        Assert.Contains(\"deltaCenter\", html, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        Assert.Contains(\"label.setAttribute('transform',\", html, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n    }\n\n    // === live per-node status overlay (issue #219) =====================================\n    //\n    // While a `guardrails run` is in progress, diagram.html gains a small corner-anchored status\n    // badge on each task container, preflight/guardrail leaf, and the plan-level Full Flight Checks\n    // / Terminal Gate brackets: an animated spinner while running, a settled check/X/\"?\" glyph once\n    // finished — driven by an OPTIONAL per-node status map plus an INDEPENDENT includeRefresh\n    // toggle, mirroring LogSiteRenderer.IndexHtml(..., includeRefresh)'s during-run/final duality.\n    //\n    // These tests are structural/string-content assertions over the emitted HTML/JS (no headless\n    // browser is configured in this repo — a documented Level-A gap): they prove the right markup\n    // and data are EMITTED, not that a browser positions the badges pixel-correctly at runtime. The\n    // four non-null-status tests are the intended TDD RED against the throwing stub — the\n    // 02-implement-diagram-status-overlay-renderer task turns them green.\n    //\n    // Status-map ids use the SAME vocabulary MermaidRenderer emits (task containers `task_<base>`,\n    // preflight/guardrail leaves `task_<base>_pf_<n>`/`task_<base>_gr_<n>`, and the two plan-level\n    // brackets `plan_preflights`/`plan_guardrails`) so the post-render overlay script can position a\n    // badge on the matching SVG node. All five status values are exercised.\n    private static readonly IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string> SampleStatuses =\n        new Dictionary<string, string>(StringComparer.Ordinal)\n        {\n            [\"plan_preflights\"] = \"passed\",       // Full Flight Checks bracket (top)\n            [\"task_root\"] = \"running\",            // a task container, mid-run -> spinner\n            [\"task_root_pf_0\"] = \"passed\",        // a preflight leaf check\n            [\"task_root_gr_0\"] = \"failed\",        // a guardrail leaf check\n            [\"task_next\"] = \"pending\",            // a not-yet-started task container\n            [\"plan_guardrails\"] = \"needs-human\",  // Terminal Gate bracket (bottom)\n        };\n\n    [Fact]\n    public void Render_WithNullNodeStatuses_IsByteIdenticalToCurrentBehavior()\n    {\n        // The static `graph` command path (no live status) must be UNCHANGED by this feature: the\n        // pre-existing three-argument overload and the new call passing nodeStatuses:null must\n        // produce the exact same document, byte-for-byte — the golden fixtures\n        // (examples/hello-guardrails, docs/plans/08-parallel-execution/diagram.html) are out of this\n        // task's scope and must not need regenerating.\n        string legacy = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, OneTarget);\n        string newNull = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, OneTarget, nodeStatuses: null);\n\n        Assert.Equal(legacy, newNull);\n\n        // ...and the static path carries NONE of the live-overlay markers. Each of these is absent\n        // from today's template, so their absence pins the null path clean — a leak of the feature\n        // into the static path (which would silently change every checked-in diagram.html) fails here.\n        Assert.DoesNotContain(\"http-equiv=\\\"refresh\\\"\", newNull, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        Assert.DoesNotContain(\"@keyframes\", newNull, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        Assert.DoesNotContain(\"id=\\\"node-statuses\\\"\", newNull, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n    }\n\n    [Fact]\n    public void Render_WithNodeStatuses_EmitsAMetaRefreshTag()\n    {\n        // A non-null status map with the default includeRefresh:true is the DURING-RUN diagram — it\n        // must carry <meta http-equiv=\"refresh\"> so a plain file:// view re-reads itself as the run\n        // progresses (mirrors LogSiteRenderer's during-run index). The static (null) path must not.\n        string live = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, OneTarget, SampleStatuses);\n        Assert.Contains(\"<meta http-equiv=\\\"refresh\\\"\", live, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n\n        string stat = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, OneTarget, nodeStatuses: null);\n        Assert.DoesNotContain(\"http-equiv=\\\"refresh\\\"\", stat, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n    }\n\n    [Fact]\n    public void Render_WithNodeStatusesAndIncludeRefreshFalse_OmitsTheMetaRefreshTag()\n    {\n        // The FINAL settled render (wired at run-end by 06-wire-diagramobserver-into-runcommand):\n        // nodeStatuses is STILL non-null (every node shows its final settled status) but\n        // includeRefresh:false, so the auto-reload tag is dropped — the page is done refreshing. The\n        // status overlay itself must STILL be emitted (the refresh tag and the overlay are independent).\n        string settled = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(\n            Source, Hash, OneTarget, SampleStatuses, includeRefresh: false);\n\n        Assert.DoesNotContain(\"http-equiv=\\\"refresh\\\"\", settled, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        // still a live-status document — the overlay data is present regardless of includeRefresh.\n        Assert.Contains(\"id=\\\"node-statuses\\\"\", settled, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        Assert.Contains(\"\\\"task_root\\\"\", settled, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n    }\n\n    [Fact]\n    public void Render_WithNodeStatuses_EmitsAnOverlayForEachStatusEntry()\n    {\n        // Every node id in the status map must be referenced by the overlay-rendering logic — the\n        // map is embedded as a JSON side-table (mirroring the task-folder-targets side-table) keyed\n        // by the SAME Mermaid node/container ids, so the post-render script can position a badge on\n        // each matching SVG node. Assert the QUOTED (JSON-key) form: a bare-word check would false-\n        // positive on ids like `plan_guardrails` that ALREADY appear in a code comment in today's\n        // template — only the emitted status map produces the quoted form.\n        string live = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, OneTarget, SampleStatuses);\n\n        foreach (string nodeId in SampleStatuses.Keys)\n        {\n            Assert.Contains($\"\\\"{nodeId}\\\"\", live, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        }\n    }\n\n    [Fact]\n    public void Render_WithRunningStatus_EmitsASpinnerClass_AndSettledStatusesEmitAGlyph()\n    {\n        // \"running\" must render an ANIMATED spinner (a CSS @keyframes rotation — no external\n        // image/GIF dependency), visibly distinct from a settled status's STATIC glyph (check / X /\n        // \"?\"). Assert both the spinner animation + its dedicated class AND at least one settled\n        // glyph are present; the spinner marker (a CSS class) is inherently distinct from the glyph\n        // characters, so a spinner can never be mistaken for a settled state.\n        string live = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, OneTarget, SampleStatuses);\n\n        // spinner: a CSS keyframes rotation + a dedicated class (neither exists in the static template).\n        Assert.Contains(\"@keyframes\", live, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        Assert.Contains(\"status-spinner\", live, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n\n        // settled glyphs: `passed` -> U+2713 CHECK MARK, `failed` -> U+2717 BALLOT X (both present in\n        // SampleStatuses). \\u escapes, not literal glyphs, keep this source pure-ASCII and unambiguous.\n        Assert.Contains(\"✓\", live, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        Assert.Contains(\"✗\", live, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n    }\n}\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":450,"oldLines":7,"newStart":450,"newLines":8,"lines":["         Assert.Contains(\"status-spinner\", live, StringComparison.Ordinal);"," ","         // settled glyphs: `passed` -> U+2713 CHECK MARK, `failed` -> U+2717 BALLOT X (both present in","-        // SampleStatuses). \\u escapes, not literal glyphs, keep this source pure-ASCII and unambiguous.","+        // SampleStatuses). ## Task

**Scope boundary (harness-enforced):** Write only to
`tests/Guardrails.Core.Tests/HtmlDiagramRendererTests.cs` and
`src/Guardrails.Core/Graph/HtmlDiagramRenderer.cs` (the stub file). After this task
completes, the harness runs a `git diff` check and rejects any edit outside these
paths — including changes to other production files, neighbouring test files, or the
`.csproj`. An out-of-scope edit fails the task immediately and consumes a retry. If you

write `{"needsHuman": "<what is missing>"}` to the state-out path and stop.

### Background

`src/Guardrails.Core/Graph/HtmlDiagramRenderer.cs` currently exposes:

```csharp
public static string Render(
    string mermaidSource, string sourceHash, IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string> taskFolderTargets)
```

It returns the full `diagram.html` document — a Mermaid-rendered DAG with pan/zoom, a
`#legend` overlay, and a title-band click overlay per task container (all corner-anchored
`<div>`s positioned outside the Mermaid SVG, or embedded scripts that compute positions
from the SVG after Mermaid renders — see the existing `#legend` div and the
`addTaskContainerOverlays` function in the file for the exact technique to mirror).

This plan (issue #219) adds a LIVE STATUS OVERLAY: while a `guardrails run` is in
progress, `diagram.html` should show a small corner-anchored status badge on each task
container, preflight-check leaf, guardrail-check leaf, and the plan-level "Full Flight
Checks"/"Terminal Gate" brackets — an animated spinner while running, a settled icon
(check / X / "?") once finished — updated by re-rendering the file as the run
progresses (a separate task, `03-author-tests-diagram-observer`, builds the harness-side
piece that calls this rendering capability after each event; THIS task is scope to the
rendering capability itself, in isolation, driven directly with an in-memory status map).

### What to build (tests + stubs only — no real implementation)

1. **A new overload/parameters on `HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render`** that accept an OPTIONAL
   per-node status map AND an independent refresh-tag toggle, e.g.:

   ```csharp
   public static string Render(
       string mermaidSource, string sourceHash, IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string> taskFolderTargets,
       IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string>? nodeStatuses = null, bool includeRefresh = true)
   ```

   where `nodeStatuses` maps a Mermaid node/container id (the same ids already used
   throughout this file and `MermaidRenderer.cs` — task container ids, preflight/guardrail
   leaf ids, the plan-level bracket ids) to a status string: `"pending"`, `"running"`,
   `"passed"`, `"failed"`, or `"needs-human"`. Existing callers that omit both parameters
   (the static `graph` command, which never runs live) must be unaffected — `Render`
   with `nodeStatuses: null` (or omitted) must produce **byte-identical** output to
   today's `Render`, since the golden fixtures (`examples/hello-guardrails/...`,
   `docs/plans/08-parallel-execution/diagram.html`) are not part of this task's scope
   and must not need regenerating.

   **The refresh tag and the status overlay are INDEPENDENT** — mirror
   `src/Guardrails.Cli/Ui/LogSiteRenderer.cs`'s own `IndexHtml(..., includeRefresh: bool)`
   parameter shape, which the same during-run/final duality already uses for the log
   site: the DURING-RUN diagram (`nodeStatuses` non-null, `includeRefresh: true`, the
   default) carries the refresh tag; the FINAL settled diagram (`nodeStatuses` non-null
   — still showing each node's final settled status — but `includeRefresh: false`) must
   NOT carry it. A later task (`06-wire-diagramobserver-into-runcommand`) wires a final,
   no-refresh render at run-end, mirroring `RunCommand.cs`'s existing
   `LogSiteRenderer.ExportSite` end-of-run call for the log site — that wiring depends on
   this `includeRefresh` parameter existing.
2. **When `nodeStatuses` is provided**, the emitted HTML must additionally carry:
   - A per-node overlay badge `<div>` (or an embedded JS function that creates one per
     entry in `nodeStatuses`), positioned via `getBBox()`/`getBoundingClientRect()` on
     the corresponding SVG node, recomputed on every `svg-pan-zoom` pan/zoom event (the
     already-loaded `svg-pan-zoom` instance exposes `onPan`/`onZoom` callbacks — mirror
     how the existing title-band overlay code in this file already hooks post-render).
     A `"running"` status renders a spinner (a simple CSS `@keyframes` rotation is
     sufficient — do not add an external image/GIF dependency); a settled status renders
     a plain check/X/"?" glyph. This applies REGARDLESS of `includeRefresh`.
   - A `<meta http-equiv="refresh" content="2">` tag in `<head>`, if AND ONLY IF
     `nodeStatuses` is non-null AND `includeRefresh` is `true` (the default) — so a
     plain `file://` view re-reads itself with no server needed during a live run. When
     `nodeStatuses` is null/omitted (the static, one-shot `graph` command path), or when
     `includeRefresh` is explicitly `false` (the final settled render), this tag must be
     ABSENT.
3. **Write the MINIMAL stub** in `HtmlDiagramRenderer.cs`: the new parameters exist and
   compile, but the status-overlay logic can `throw new NotImplementedException()` (or
   return a placeholder) when `nodeStatuses is not null` — the test-author task's job is
   to make the TESTS compile and FAIL, not to implement the feature.
4. **Write the tests** in `HtmlDiagramRendererTests.cs` (xUnit — this repo's existing
   framework; mirror the existing test style in this same file: string-content
   assertions over the returned HTML, no browser driver). At minimum:
   - `Render_WithNullNodeStatuses_IsByteIdenticalToCurrentBehavior` — calling `Render`
     without the new parameters (or with `nodeStatuses: null`) produces the exact same
     string as before this change (paste a known-good fixture, or call the pre-existing
     overload shape and assert equality with the new call passing `nodeStatuses: null`).
   - `Render_WithNodeStatuses_EmitsAMetaRefreshTag` — passing a non-null `nodeStatuses`
     (default `includeRefresh: true`) causes `<meta http-equiv="refresh"` to appear;
     passing `null` does not.
   - `Render_WithNodeStatusesAndIncludeRefreshFalse_OmitsTheMetaRefreshTag` — passing a
     non-null `nodeStatuses` with `includeRefresh: false` still emits the status
     overlay/badges but does NOT emit `<meta http-equiv="refresh"`.
   - `Render_WithNodeStatuses_EmitsAnOverlayForEachStatusEntry` — for each key in a
     sample `nodeStatuses` map, the emitted HTML/script contains a reference to that
     node id in the overlay-rendering logic (a structural/string-content assertion —
     e.g. the node id appears inside the embedded status-map JSON or a generated JS
     data structure the overlay script reads).
   - `Render_WithRunningStatus_EmitsASpinnerClass_AndSettledStatusesEmitAGlyph` — the
     word "running" (or your chosen CSS class name) maps to a distinguishable
     spinner-shaped element/class in the output, distinct from a settled status's glyph.

   These tests must **compile** against the stub and **fail** when run (a legitimate
   `NotImplementedException`/assertion failure) — that failure IS the TDD red the
   `02-implement-diagram-status-overlay-renderer` task turns green.

### Note on browser-based verification (Level A gap)

No headless-browser driver (Playwright/Cypress) is configured in this repo, so these
tests are structural/string-content assertions on the generated HTML/JS — they prove
the right markup and data are EMITTED, not that a browser actually renders correct,
error-free positioning at runtime. This gap is intentional and documented in the
breakdown report; do not attempt to add a browser-driver dependency to close it here.

function Test-Escapes([string]$candidate) {
    if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($candidate)) { return $false }

    if (-not [System.IO.Path]::IsPathRooted($candidate)) {

    return -not $resolved.StartsWith($rootFull + [System.IO.Path]::DirectorySeparatorChar, [StringComparison]::OrdinalIgnoreCase)

## Root cause of the prior failure (now avoided)

Attempt 1 actually produced correct red/green tests, but the *then-current* guardrail-02 used a brittle regex `Passed:\s*\d+,\s*Failed:\s*[1-9]` expecting `Passed: N, Failed: M` field order — the opposite of what VSTest emits (`Failed: M, Passed: N`) — so it false-negatived even with genuinely-failing tests (attempt 2 diagnosed exactly this). The guardrail has since been **fixed** to a direct exit-code check, so redoing attempt 1's clean approach against the fixed guardrail passes. My work is confined to the two in-scope files.

- Null path is **completely untouched** → byte-identical static output. Non-null path throws `NotImplementedException` (the deliberate red). `includeRefresh` is referenced in the guard so every new parameter is "used" (build stays warning-clean under `TreatWarningsAsErrors`).
